note: The dated change log on /bitcoin-inheritance-planning, in the shape of lenderLog.json (lenders v2 C, JM's rulings 2026-10-01): a What changed section above the cards, a badge on a card whose newest provider change is under 14 days old, and each card's Changes logged line. Seeded with the provider changes the 24-26 Nov 2026 research found with exact, sourced dates; undated changes are left out. Every re-read is logged even when nothing moved. Entries may go in any order: inheritanceLogIndex.js sorts them by date. kind: 'check' (a re-read of the cards; give read and changed counts; plans: [...] when it covered only some) | 'page' (a card added, removed or brought into line with the provider's pages: type added | removed | updated) | 'provider' (something the provider changed: type launch | terms | price | availability | exit). plan: the card id in inheritance.json; the build fails on an unknown id. source: the provider's own page for the change where there is one. changes (optional): [{field, was}] with field one of wait, heir, without, renew, steps, price, keys, keep, gone, identity, beneficiary, probate, time, documents; the card highlights those lines for 14 days. Procedure: MONTHLY_REFRESH_CHECKLIST §7.7.

entries.text: Page published with seventeen cards in three groups, each read against the provider’s own pages on 25 and 26 November 2026. Lines a provider doesn’t publish are marked “not published” on the card.

First reading: all seventeen cards checked line by line against each provider’s own pages. Three items the research had carried as open are now on the providers’ pages: Casa’s death-certificate route (Private Client), Nunchuk’s 7- or 30-day buffer (off-chain plans), and the day AnchorWatch’s recovery path opens (day 335, insured). The rest stay “not published”.

AnchorWatch Trust Company opened as a Nevada-chartered qualified custodian, with fixed-dollar custody fees by vault size (press: The Block). AnchorWatch’s own pricing page, read on 26 November, shows flat monthly fees for its vaults, capped at $1,000 a month for individuals and small businesses; its FAQ still quotes the older 0.02% a month.
Strike launched beneficiary plans: up to 15 beneficiaries, or a trust, under a transfer-on-death agreement signed in the app, for US individuals and sole proprietors outside Louisiana.
Nunchuk 2.0 added an on-chain inheritance option: after the date you set, a spending path that doesn’t need Nunchuk’s key, with a kit for heirs to claim alone.
